benchmark_notes: Five alternating pairs per case. Medians are local elapsed timings, not a cross-machine guarantee. Trace peaks include NumPy allocations but are not process RSS.

Read timing excludes hashing/tracemalloc. Hash covers array names, shapes, dtypes, bytes and window/batch instructions. Cached filesystem; one whole episode is still decoded, no mmap/asynchronous reader.

Read-complete measures final read/batch functions. Raster/reset/H1 snapshots exactly match final corresponding source files. Successful pool paths are unchanged by later exception-combination hardening; pipeline-complete uses the exact final recorder snapshot.

Owned endurance processes were stopped/resumed with verified PID identities during isolated performance measurements; their wall durations include these pauses. Other machine activity was not controlled.

Pipeline includes NumPy physics, raster images, recorder append and final close/drain; excludes environment/writer construction and subsequent correctness audit. Queued payload can exceed the synchronous retained payload while remaining inside the shared 256 MiB budget. Stack/compression scratch and Python objects are extra.
Synthetic noise isolates high-entropy compression and is not physical camera data. Raster data uses the CPU debug scene, not robot photorealistic rendering.

H1 random-action training-mode step benchmark has two physics threads and drops ten warmup steps. CPU physical state, observations, reward terms and flags are bit-identical over 1200 steps for each batch size. Tiny large-batch timing differences are not a meaningful optimization claim.

training_equivalence.scope: Correctness only; paired 100-update training on CPU Torch2.13; concurrent recorder endurance makes elapsed timings unsuitable for performance claims

cross_version_resume.note: Policy/Adam compatibility with environment/RNG restart; this does not claim exact continuation across Torch versions.

exclusions: Exploratory pipeline/reset runs overlapped edits or other owned benchmarks; only frozen, sequential/isolated final variants are used for timing claims.
Removing the H1 previous-velocity copy changed array layout and raw acceleration reduction rounding for batches > 1. It was rejected and the copy retained; final H1 trajectory hashes all match.

The first endurance fixture assumed every reset started outside the success radius. It was corrected to verify the actual active transition count; that short exploratory failure was not a recorder defect.
Shuffled long-history reads showed roughly unchanged runtime; no shuffled-throughput gain is claimed. Legacy full episode reads also show no meaningful speedup.
No additional Microduck training-quality study was conducted in round two. The first report retains its limited single-seed 751-update evidence, mixed tracking result and incomplete multi-seed study.
